name: d121_32order
notes: The design-121 32-order Dammann fan through the staged pipeline, end to end: the DOE's own order table -> 32 independent traced chains to the fine-retrace exit -> one common carrier -> one leg plan -> 32 Bluestein zooms. ray_subsample=1 is this pipeline's default and is the configuration PROBE_CHAIN_LADDER_PISTON S2.4 recommends for an aggregating consumer: rs=4 throws away 6.5e-03 of the aperture power, 160x the campaign's 4e-05 energy bar, and no affordable grid refinement recovers it as cheaply. n_fine_cap=8192 is the affordable grid of record (ADJUDICATION_NFC_8192); the pre-flight PROVES the RAM clamp cannot bind and the runner asserts the grid it got. n_common=8192 at 1.2292 um is a 10.07 mm window, which holds all 32 chief rays (-1.915..+1.436 mm in x) plus their 2.64 mm support with 0.48 mm to spare -- the tightest beam is the same (-4,-2) the probe measured. capture_reference_tile keeps each chain's own shipped-path tile, which is what the per-frame comparison is scored against. LEG MODE: 'crop' is the like-for-like variant against the shipped per-order path and is what the run of record used. BUILD_PIPELINE_2026_08_11 S6.4 then MEASURED that at 32 orders the 4.74 mm crop cuts the fan's own neighbours mid-aperture and their diffraction lands in the frame: worst |P/P_shipped - 1| = 2.384e-04 against the campaign's 4e-05 bar, with every ratio ABOVE 1. On the same summed field and the same frames the 'full' leg -- the architecture as specified, which truncates nothing -- reads 2.641e-05 and holds every bar. Set leg.mode='full' for a FILLED fan; 'crop' is right only for a sparse subset.
